title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: When Goods Fit Their Category at the Review Decision
content:
## Clause

Under Dangerous Goods Acceptance, goods fit their category for the purpose of a review decision only when every test the decision itself applies to the acceptance and to its carrying booking is passed, on the records as they stand at the decision. Failing any single one of those tests means the goods do not fit.

Those tests are the complete basis on which fit is judged at the decision. Two further groups of conditions belong to admission, not to the decision:

- the booking mix and the customer's allotment on the sailing, which are counted when an application or an amendment is admitted and are not counted a second time when the review is decided;
- the conditions about the applicant and its booking arrangements — contract rating, the age of the customer profile, the misdeclaration block, the waiting period after a rejection and the placing of limited-quantity goods — which are examined at admission and are left alone when the review is decided.

## Truth table

| All decision tests passed | Any decision test failed | Goods fit |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes |
| no | yes | no |

## Points of judgement

**Since admission the sailing has filled with the same customer's other acceptances. Does that change the fit?** No; the sailing allotment is not re-counted at the decision.

**The customer's profile would no longer satisfy a tenure test today. Is the fit affected?** No; applicant conditions were settled at admission.
